status: proposed investment grouping; Core is the working recommendation
headline: Invest in six connected changes to the King’s experience
standfirst: The proposed V2 case follows the six-project mobilisation plan. It gives each project a clear investment purpose while retaining the established Economy, Core and Enhanced financial options. The Graduate Futures pool is attributed jointly to Insight and Reputation until its mixed costs can be apportioned.

projects.investmentPurpose: Give every student a supported conversation about purpose, a living language for their capabilities and a trustworthy fuller account of learning.
projects.whyThisInvestment: Funds practitioner discovery and student co-design, deep trailblazers in purpose and skills, record prototyping and the capabilities needed to carry proven models into normal practice.
projects.yearOne: Test the purpose proposition, build the first skills proof of concept and prototype approaches to trusted recognition.

stories.label: Student
stories.text: I can understand what matters to me, recognise what my discipline and wider experiences are helping me develop, and evidence that learning credibly as I consider my next move.

stories.label: Academic / programme team
stories.text: I can connect the distinctive capabilities of my discipline to the wider developmental journey without turning my course into generic employability training.

stories.label: The University
stories.text: We have a tested language for purpose, capabilities and trusted recognition that connects educational philosophy to experience and transition across King’s Edge.

projects.investmentPurpose: Make good experiential learning a clearer educational expectation within and near the curriculum.
projects.whyThisInvestment: Combines North Star design and co-creation with targeted curriculum implementation and reusable formal routes, including sandwich years and the Level 6 capstone.
projects.yearOne: Agree the North Star and future entitlement direction, identify curriculum growth priorities and validate the first shared formal pathways.

stories.label: Student
stories.text: I can expect to apply, test and extend my learning through meaningful experience in or alongside my course, not only if my course already happens to offer it.

stories.label: Course team
stories.text: I can act on evidence that experiential learning is weak or uneven in my programme and get practical support to strengthen it.

stories.label: Academic / educator
stories.text: I can build purposeful experiential learning into my teaching using tested models and shared support, without inventing the delivery route from scratch.

stories.label: Faculty / professional staff
stories.text: We can move good ideas into delivery more quickly because policy, validation and administrative routes have already been worked through.

stories.label: The University
stories.text: We can make meaningful experiential learning a more dependable part of a King’s education and target investment where students currently have the least access.

projects.investmentPurpose: Turn UK, international and civic relationships into accessible opportunity, and support graduates proactively through transition.
projects.whyThisInvestment: Funds a staged UK and international opportunity-development capability, Global Mobility growth, beyond-course commissioning and the Graduate Transitions service. Student Opportunities Fund awards need a separate funding decision.
projects.yearOne: Protect live international employer relationships, start Global Mobility development, design access funding and commission the first £150k opportunity portfolio.

stories.label: Student
stories.text: I can build a sequence of experiences over time, from trying something new through to sustained projects, mentoring, placements and deeper opportunities that help me make a purposeful transition.

stories.label: External partner / alumnus
stories.text: I have a clear route into King’s and can turn an idea into a meaningful student opportunity without navigating multiple disconnected teams.

stories.label: International student / graduate
stories.text: I can access employer relationships, labour-market insight and purposeful global experience relevant to the markets in which I may want to live and work.

stories.label: Graduate
stories.text: King’s does not disappear at graduation if I am struggling to make the transition. I can be identified and supported through that next step.

stories.label: The University
stories.text: We can actively shape the opportunity environment, commissioning more supply and deeper experiences where evidence shows that students need them most.

stories.label: The University
stories.text: We have one coherent route connecting employer and civic relationships, opportunity infrastructure, access funding, commissioning and graduate transition to the wider developmental architecture.

projects.investmentPurpose: Make the wider King’s experience visible, inclusive and well timed for different patterns of student life.
projects.whyThisInvestment: Builds the Beyond Course shopfront and participation evidence, tests Student Life designs and establishes a coherent annual student-journey rhythm. Subject societies remain deferred without a funded mobilisation ask.
projects.yearOne: Launch a live Beyond Course evidence base and shopfront, test participation personas and prototypes, and map the institutional rhythm.

stories.label: Student
stories.text: I can see and take part in worthwhile opportunities that fit around the realities of my life and study, including commuting, caring, paid work or limited time on campus.

stories.label: Opportunity provider
stories.text: I can change my provision when the evidence shows who is missing, where participation drops away or where an experience is not producing the value we intended.

stories.label: The University
stories.text: We can see gaps in participation and the wider student-year rhythm, then work with commissioners and providers to make the opportunity environment more inclusive.

projects.investmentPurpose: Give course and service teams usable graduate-futures evidence, external challenge and a targeted outcomes improvement cycle.
projects.whyThisInvestment: Supports course-level data packs and sense-making, employer and alumni validation, Graduate Outcomes response optimisation and priority survey strategy. The shared analytics allocation sits here.
projects.yearOne: Test the first course packs, establish external validation and run a focused Graduate Outcomes response pilot.

stories.label: Student
stories.text: I can use a clearer account of what my course and wider experience are helping me develop to make decisions, describe my strengths and prepare for what comes next.

stories.label: Course team
stories.text: I can act earlier when evidence shows that students are not getting the graduate value we expect, and test whether the changes we make are improving the experience.

stories.label: Faculty leader
stories.text: I can direct attention and resource towards the programmes or cohorts where the evidence shows the greatest need or opportunity.

stories.label: The University
stories.text: We can close the loop between student experience, graduate outcomes and educational improvement, using external challenge and course evidence to act rather than merely report.

projects.investmentPurpose: Turn credible graduate-premium evidence into claims that students and external audiences recognise and use.
projects.whyThisInvestment: Creates evidence-backed content assets and tests student adoption and external activation. The combined activation, research and survey-intervention envelope is accounted for once here, alongside the programme-controlled Strategic Partnerships, Profile and External Engagement Fund.
projects.yearOne: Produce the first proof points and exemplars, test the student proposition and run limited external message tests.

stories.label: Student
stories.text: I can recognise and explain the value of my King’s education through credible examples of my course and wider development.

stories.label: Recruitment / reputation colleague
stories.text: I can make stronger claims about the value of a King’s education using credible evidence and examples that stand up to scrutiny, beyond rankings or a conventional careers-service claim.

stories.label: The University
stories.text: We can test whether evidence-backed graduate-premium messages resonate with students and external audiences before extending them.

investmentChoices.title: Economy
investmentChoices.description: Establish the architecture with narrower UK brokerage, two-post international coverage, one Global Mobility development post and a single graduate-transition coach. Opportunity and implementation reach are constrained.

investmentChoices.title: Core
investmentChoices.description: Fund the staged four-post UK team, full international regional team by January 2029, two Global Mobility posts and a G7/G6 Graduate Transitions team from September 2028, matched to the £150k / £200k / £250k opportunity portfolio.

investmentChoices.title: Enhanced
investmentChoices.description: Accelerate employer, Global Mobility and Graduate Transitions capacity and support a substantially larger opportunity and implementation portfolio.

accountingNotes: The five accounting pools cover six V2 projects because the V1 Graduate Futures package mixes insight, evidence assets, surveys and activation. Its £764.8k Core total is held once until a defensible allocation between projects 2.5 and 2.6 is agreed.

The combined activation, research and survey-intervention cash envelope of £25k / £35k / £50k is held once under V2 student and external activation. Shared analytics FTE is assigned to outcomes and survey improvement.
The £25k / £35k / £45k Strategic Partnerships, Profile and External Engagement Fund is programme controlled and held once under activation, even when it supports work elsewhere.
A new Student Opportunities Fund award pot is outside this mobilisation ask. The Digital Student Experience Hub has a separate institutional investment case.
The July 2029 onwards Core commissioning requirement of £175k a year and other recurrent exposure are BAU planning liabilities, not a fourth mobilisation year.
